findings.title: Destructive `<<` mutates string and misbehaves
findings.detail: `". " << website_host` is a mutation of a string literal; with frozen string literals this raises FrozenError, and the intent is awkward. Also the check `discourse_host.ends_with?("." + website_host)` differs from the sibling comparison logic. Use non-mutating concatenation.

findings.title: Sibling-domain heuristic compares only equal label counts, wrong for multi-part TLDs
findings.detail: Hosts with the same number of labels are treated as related if everything after the first label matches. This fails with different subdomain depths (e.g. www.example.com vs a.b.example.com) and misclassifies other combos. The sibling branch also depends on label count heuristics rather than registrable domains.

findings.title: Inline rescue swallows all errors and URI re-parsed repeatedly
findings.detail: `rescue nil` modifier hides all StandardErrors. URI(website.to_s).path is re-parsed several times, and a non-http URI such as mailto: or javascript: could produce a nil host or path. For URIs with a host but nil/opaque path, `website_host + path` can raise TypeError.

findings.title: include_website_name defined without trailing '?' so never used
findings.detail: ActiveModel::Serializers calls include_<attr>?; the method name `include_website_name` lacks the `?` so it is never invoked, and website_name is always included (nil for blank). Also, untrusted-user restriction on website is not applied to website_name, leaking info for anonymous viewing of TL0 users.

findings.title: website_name nil when website host is unparsable removes display of website
findings.detail: Previously the name was derived from split('/')[2] for any non-empty website, e.g. schemeless inputs. Now URI('example.com').host is nil so the website link disappears from the profile entirely.

findings.title: Tests miss the sibling-subdomain branch and the untrusted attribute case
findings.detail: No test covers the equal-label-count branch (www.example.com vs forum.example.com) nor the invalid URL case; the untrusted attribute list was not updated with website_name.

findings.title: include_website_name lacks '?' so it is never called by the serializer
findings.detail: ActiveModel::Serializers conditionally includes attributes via `include_<attr>?`. Defining `include_website_name` without a question mark means the filter is ignored. website_name is always serialized, even when the website is blank or restricted for untrusted users (website is in untrusted_attributes).

findings.title: String#<< mutates a literal, wrongly builds the suffix
findings.detail: `"." << website_host` mutates the literal "." and yields ".example.com". This only works when string literals are not frozen, and it raises FrozenError otherwise. `ends_with?("." + website_host)` would be correct and safe.

findings.title: Sibling-subdomain heuristic compares only labels after the first, which can match unrelated domains
findings.detail: For equal-length hostnames with more than 2 labels, only the first label is dropped and the rest compared. This matches wrong cases, such as a.b.c.co.uk versus x.b.c.co.uk. It also misses same-site cases where the label counts differ. Behaviour is inconsistent with the comment 'www.example.com == forum.example.com'.

findings.title: Host/path handling can crash or misbehave on nil/odd values
findings.detail: The `rescue nil` modifier hides errors for the host only, while `URI(website.to_s).path` is later called unprotected. Websites without a scheme (e.g. 'example.com') yield a nil host, so no name is shown where the old client code showed something. Discourse.current_hostname may also be nil in some contexts, which would crash on split/ends_with?.

findings.title: Tests miss sibling-subdomain branch and the include filter
findings.detail: The spec only covers three branches (different domain, same domain, parent domain). It doesn't test the same-length sibling-subdomain branch, a blank website, or a website without a scheme. The `include_website_name` bug goes undetected.

findings.detail: ActiveModel::Serializers looks up include_<attr>? for conditional attributes. Defining include_website_name (no question mark) means it is never consulted, so website_name is always serialized. It also bypasses the untrusted-attribute restriction that hides website for TL0 users seen by anonymous, so the hostname leaks.

findings.detail: Comparing everything after the first label only when label counts are equal is fragile. For example, a.co.uk and b.co.uk both reduce to co.uk and are treated as the same site, and the rule fails for differing label counts. The comment says www.example.com == forum.example.com, but the branch also covers any same-depth hosts.

findings.title: Fragile URI parsing with rescue modifier, and path may be nil or an unwanted value
findings.detail: `rescue nil` swallows all errors silently. For a website value without a scheme (e.g. 'example.com'), URI() gives a nil host, so no name is shown at all, which the old split('/')[2] logic also failed on. URI(...) is also re-parsed repeatedly. A trailing path of '/' is appended, producing 'example.com/' for same-host sites.

findings.title: Validation has side effects: match stats updated on every validity check
findings.detail: should_block? is called from the email validator, and User#valid? runs more than once per signup (create calls user.valid? then user.save). Each call increments match_count and writes to the DB, so counts are inflated and the write is a side effect of validation.

findings.title: Blocked email lookup is case-sensitive and not normalized
findings.detail: BlockedEmail.where(email: email) is an exact match. A blocked address can be bypassed by changing the case (Bad@Spam.com) or by whitespace, so the block list is trivially evaded.

findings.title: Non-atomic read-modify-write of match_count
findings.detail: match_count is incremented in Ruby and then saved, so concurrent signups with the same email lose updates. An atomic increment (update_all/increment_counter) should be used.

findings.title: rejectedEmails array shared across all controller instances
findings.detail: Em.A([]) in the class body is created once and is shared by every instance of the controller (prototype property). Rejected emails persist across modal uses and instances, and the array is mutated in place.

findings.title: Email regexp match fails on nil value and domain setting is unescaped
findings.detail: The whitelist/blacklist regexp is built from a raw site setting with only '.' escaped, and the regexp is unanchored at the end, so 'example.com' also matches 'example.com.evil.org' and 'bar.com' matches 'bar.community'. Other regex metacharacters in the setting are interpreted too.

findings.title: Validator spec doesn't exercise the integration or the whitelist/blacklist paths
findings.detail: The validator is constructed with attributes: :email (not an array) and only the stubbed BlockedEmail branch is tested. The moved whitelist/blacklist logic has no coverage, and the stubs hide real behaviour.

findings.title: Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive and bypassable
findings.detail: BlockedEmail.where(email: email) is an exact match, so a blocked address can be bypassed by changing case (Bad@Spam.com vs bad@spam.com). The email is not normalized before lookup or storage.

findings.title: Validator mutates stats on every validation and non-atomically
findings.detail: should_block? is called from a validator, so every valid?/save/user.valid? call (create calls valid? then save) increments match_count and last_match_at, double-counting. The read-modify-write is also racy under concurrent requests; use an atomic increment.

findings.title: Whitelist/blacklist check fails on nil value and matches unanchored domain
findings.detail: The regexp is built from the setting without anchoring the end or escaping other regexp characters, so a whitelisted 'example.com' also matches 'user@example.com.evil.org'. Domains with '|' or other regex metacharacters are interpreted as regex.

findings.title: Shared mutable array on controller prototype
findings.detail: Em.A([]) in the extend() hash is shared by all instances of the controller, so rejected emails persist across instances and can leak between sessions.

findings.title: Wrong dependent key for array observation
findings.detail: 'rejectedEmails.@each' is not a valid dependent key for an Ember array (should be 'rejectedEmails.[]' or '@each.prop'), so the emailValidation may not recompute when an email is pushed.

findings.title: Rejected email added to client list for any email error
findings.detail: The client adds the email to rejectedEmails for any error on email (including taken or format), and the response echoes attributes. The rejected email is also shown as 'invalid' rather than the server's reason. Any email error, even transient, permanently marks it as rejected.

findings.title: Validation has side effects: stats updated on every validity check
findings.detail: should_block? writes match_count and last_match_at, and is called from EmailValidator during validation. In UsersController#create, user.valid? and user.save both run validations, so one signup attempt increments the counter twice. Validation should not write to the database.

findings.title: Case-sensitive exact match lets blocked emails be bypassed
findings.detail: The lookup is an exact string match with no downcasing or normalization. A blocked address can be bypassed by changing case, e.g. Bad@Spam.com, or by adding whitespace.

findings.title: Non-atomic read-modify-write counter
findings.detail: match_count is incremented in Ruby and then saved. Concurrent requests read the same value, so increments are lost. An atomic update_all or increment_counter would avoid this.

findings.title: Regex match against a possibly nil value; domains are not anchored or escaped
findings.detail: The setting is interpolated into a regex with only dots escaped, and the regex is not anchored at the end. A whitelist entry such as 'example.com' also matches '@example.com.evil.org', so the check can be bypassed. Other regex metacharacters in the setting are unescaped.

findings.title: rejectedEmails array shared across controller instances
findings.detail: Em.A([]) is created once in the class definition and is shared by every instance of the controller. It persists rejected emails across instances, and is mutated through pushObject.

findings.title: Response echoes attributes and enables blocklist probing
findings.detail: The create response returns the submitted email and the error hash. Combined with the side-effecting block check, an unauthenticated caller can probe which emails are blocked. Because failed attempts are also counted, the stats can be inflated.

findings.title: Validator spec does not cover whitelist/blacklist logic that was moved
findings.detail: The restriction logic moved into EmailValidator, but the spec only tests the blocked-email path with a stub. The domain whitelist/blacklist branches and the skip-if-already-errored branch are untested.

findings.title: Duplicate downsize definition overrides 4-arg version, breaking callers
findings.detail: The second `self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` replaces the earlier `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)`. Existing callers passing width and height now have `max_height` interpreted as `opts`, so the dimensions are just the width and the height is lost or raises an error.

findings.title: Downsize loop writes to the temp file in place, and animated GIF path breaks it
findings.detail: `OptimizedImage.downsize` is called with the same path for input and output. With a GIF and allow_animation, gifsicle uses `--resize-fit 80%`, which is not a valid dimension. `downsize_instructions` also appends `\>`, which fails for a percent-only value in some cases. A failed conversion is ignored, so the loop can silently run 5 times with no effect and the oversized file is still uploaded.

findings.title: Stale tempfile.size / content_type after in-place resize
findings.detail: The image is rewritten on disk by an external process, but the cached Tempfile size and the original content_type are reused. `tempfile.size` may not reflect the new size, so the while condition may never become false or may be wrong. Also, `[0]` frame extraction and format conversion can change the content.

findings.title: Hardcoded 10MB client limit ignores site settings, including attachments
findings.detail: The max_attachment_size_kb setting is no longer enforced on the client. The 'file too large' message now reports a fixed 10MB for all file types, so attachment limits set by admins below or above 10MB are ignored and the message may be wrong.

findings.title: Hardcoded 10MB download limit for API URL uploads
findings.detail: The configurable max_image_size_kb limit is replaced with a fixed 10MB for all types, including attachments. This lets API URL downloads of non-images be 10MB regardless of the attachment setting.

findings.title: Nil filename passed to is_image? for API URL uploads / failed download
findings.detail: If the download failed (`rescue nil`), tempfile is nil and the guard handles it, but `filename` derives from the URL without a nil check elsewhere. The existing `tempfile.size` in create_for will crash on nil after the new block is skipped.

findings.title: Duplicate downsize definition overrides 4-arg version, breaking callers
findings.detail: The second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` replaces the first one in Ruby. Existing callers passing `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` now hit the 3-positional-arg signature and receive the height as `opts` (an Integer), which breaks `opts[:force_aspect_ratio]` and `opts[:allow_animation]`.

findings.title: Downsizing loop does nothing useful and can corrupt the upload
findings.detail: The `OptimizedImage.downsize` call has its return value ignored and runs in place, with from and to being the same path. A failed or partial convert can leave a corrupt or empty file. `tempfile.size` may also be stale because of the File object's buffering. The loop then runs 5 times on non-shrinking images. Animated GIFs run through `gifsicle` with `--resize-fit 80%`, which is not a valid dimension.

findings.title: Downsize applied to any image type, and the size limit is not enforced afterwards
findings.detail: The size is only reduced for images; if the downsize fails or 5 attempts are not enough, the upload continues to Upload.create_for. That method may reject it, and the error will be confusing. `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` can also be true for SVG, which cannot be reduced by this process. In the API URL path, `filename` may be nil/blank if `tempfile` is nil.

findings.title: Hardcoded 10MB limit ignores site settings and applies to attachments
findings.detail: The client now uses a fixed 10MB limit for every type, so `max_attachment_size_kb` is no longer enforced client-side. Attachments larger than the configured limit pass validation and are only rejected by the server. If the server limit is higher than 10MB, admins can no longer raise it.

findings.title: API URL download limit hardcoded to 10MB for all upload types
findings.detail: The download cap no longer follows the configured size settings, so a site with a smaller or larger configured max gets a different effective cap for API downloads, and attachments are limited the same as images.

findings.title: Duplicate downsize definition overrides 4-arg version, breaking callers
findings.detail: The second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` replaces the earlier `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` in Ruby. Existing callers passing width and height now get the height treated as `dimensions`/opts, producing wrong or failing conversions, and the first definition is dead code.

findings.title: Downsize loop ignores failure and may leave oversized or corrupt file
findings.detail: The return value of OptimizedImage.downsize is never checked, so if convert fails (e.g. the file is not a valid image, or the imagemagick/gifsicle command errors) the loop repeats 5 times pointlessly. Oversized files then fall through to Upload.create_for. Also `tempfile.size` may be cached or stale after an external process rewrites the file.

findings.title: Downsizing applies by filename regardless of upload type and in-place resize may break formats
findings.detail: The image-reduction runs for any type (e.g. avatars/attachments with image extensions) and relies on the user-supplied filename to decide. The animated GIF branch uses gifsicle with `--resize-fit 80%`, which is not a valid dimension argument, and writes input over output in place. Non-animated downsizing with `[0]` drops extra frames.

findings.title: Hardcoded 10MB limit replaces per-type size settings
findings.detail: Client validation ignores max_attachment_size_kb (type 'attachment') and the site setting, so attachments are allowed up to 10MB regardless of configuration. The server also no longer enforces the attachment limit at this layer, and the displayed message shows a fixed value.

findings.title: API URL download limit hardcoded to 10MB
findings.detail: The download cap no longer follows the configured max size and is arbitrarily fixed, so admins cannot tighten it. Downloads up to 10MB are accepted even for non-images or when settings are lower.
